subject: Export windows, regional retention, and deletion steps for tenant audit/access logs
messages:
From: Lisa Greene <lisa.greene@acmehealth.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions about tenant log exports / retention / deletion

Hi Rohan / Marissa,

Thanks for taking this. We're doing our security diligence ahead of procurement and need clarity on how Redwood handles audit and access logs for tenants. High-level asks below — I attached a filled export request template to speed things up.

Can you confirm the following for Acme Health (tenant id: ACME-001):
- Default retention periods for access logs vs. audit (admin/config) logs; can these be extended per contract?
- What export mechanisms do you offer (one-off bulk export, continuous streaming, S3 cross-account snapshots)?
- Can we export by tenant id and by time range (UTC) and include request/actor IDs for forensics?
- Export formats and compression (CSV, NDJSON, Parquet, gzipped?) and a sample file naming convention.
- Residency mapping: if we request US-only storage, are exported artifacts produced from and stored in US regions only?
- After contract termination or data deletion request, what is the timeline for permanent deletion of hosted log copies? Do you provide a deletion attestation?

We have a SOC2 audit coming and will need a written response and a sample export (small timeframe) to validate ingestion into our SIEM.

Attach: export_request_acme_20261103.xlsx

Thanks,
Lisa
Lisa Greene
Head of Security Operations
Acme Health
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Greene <lisa.greene@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions about tenant log exports / retention / deletion

Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear checklist, and for filling out the template. I copied Marissa (who owns our export tooling) — below are the high-level answers; Marissa will follow up with exact file samples and region mapping.

Quick answers (summary):
- Default retention: access logs = 30 days, audit/admin logs = 365 days; both are configurable on enterprise contracts (we can extend retention or offer archival windows).
- Export mechanisms: one-off bulk snapshot, scheduled daily exports, and S3 cross-account deliveries (we support cross-account role-based uploads). Also HTTPS pull (signed URLs) for adhoc pulls.
- Filtering: yes — exports support tenant ID, time-range, request_id and actor_id filters.
- Formats: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) is our primary export format (gzipped). We can also provide CSV or Parquet on request; naming convention: <tenant>_audit_<YYYYMMDD>_<seq>.ndjson.gz.
- Residency: exports are produced from the region where the tenant is hosted. If you are in a US-only tenancy, exports will be produced and delivered from US regions. For enterprise Private deployments we can run in your VPC to meet residency requirements.
- Deletion: hosted log copies are removed from active storage within 7 days of a contract termination request; full permanent deletion from backups and archival store occurs within 30 days unless a longer legal hold is requested. We will provide a deletion attestation letter if required.

I'm attaching our cross-account S3 instruction doc to speed the delivery setup. Marissa — can you produce a 24-hour sample export (small window) and a tiny sample file to share with Lisa?

Thanks,
Rohan Mehta
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachments: s3_cross_account_instructions.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Greene <lisa.greene@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions about tenant log exports / retention / deletion

Hi Lisa — following up with technical detail and what we'll include in the sample. Below is what our export tool supports and notes on redaction/KMS: 

Export features and notes:
- Output schema: each NDJSON line is a JSON object with fields: timestamp (ISO8601 UTC), tenant_id, request_id, actor_id, resource, action, status, user_agent, source_ip, raw_payload (if enabled). We can remove raw_payload by default for PII minimization.
- Compression & file layout: files are gzipped NDJSON by default. For heavy analytics customers we can provide partitioned Parquet with a columnar schema.
- Searchability: exports can be restricted to specific fields (tenant_id + request_id + time range). We support incremental exports (daily deltas) or full-range snapshots.
- File naming (example): ACME-001_audit_20261103_0001.ndjson.gz; rotation index increments for multi-file exports.
- Delivery options: S3 cross-account (preferred for large exports), HTTPS endpoint with signed URL, or SFTP push. For cross-account S3 we upload to a pre-provisioned bucket/role you provide; we support server-side encryption (SSE-S3) or KMS (customer-managed key).
- Residency: when a tenant is provisioned in a US region we will run the export job in that region and upload from that region: no EU egress. For multi-region customers we can scope export to a specific region on request.
- Retention config: per our standard platform settings (access logs = 30d, audit logs = 365d) these are editable via an enterprise addendum — we can put a contractual clause for longer retention or an archival handoff cadence.
- Deletion workflow: on deletion request we remove active objects immediately and schedule a background purge of snapshots/archives. We can produce a signed deletion manifest listing objects removed.

Planned next steps from our side:
1) I'll generate a 24-hour sample (small subset) in NDJSON and attach sample_audit_log_snippet.json to this thread.
2) If you confirm delivery method (S3 vs HTTPS), we'll provision a cross-account role or deliver a test signed URL.
3) We can commit to a 5 business day SLA to deliver full-range bulk exports on contractual agreement; ad-hoc smaller snapshots are typically delivered in 1-2 business days.

Let me know which method you prefer and any extra fields you need in the file schema.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Export Services
Redwood Inference
Attachments: sample_audit_log_snippet.json
From: Lisa Greene <lisa.greene@acmehealth.com>

Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions about tenant log exports / retention / deletion

Thanks — that is very helpful. A couple follow-ups: 
- Deletion attestation: we need a formal deletion attestation that includes the object manifest and deletion timestamps (signed by Redwood). Can you confirm you can provide that within the 30-day window?
- SLA: 5 business days for full bulk export is acceptable, can you confirm that applies for exports up to 2TB compressed? If >2TB we can talk about staged deliveries.
- Legal hold: if we request a temporary hold (e.g., litigation hold) how is that handled with backups/archives?

Delivery preference: S3 cross-account (we'll provide bucket + role). Please send the role ARN and a sample policy for review.

If you can confirm the attestation and the 2TB note I'll move this to procurement. Also let's schedule a 30-minute call next week to walk the SIEM ingestion sample.

Best,
Lisa
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Greene <lisa.greene@acmehealth.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions about tenant log exports / retention / deletion

Lisa — looping in procurement follow-through and to confirm operational commitments. Quick confirmations: 
- Deletion attestation: yes, we provide a signed deletion manifest including object keys and RFC3339 deletion timestamps within 30 days of termination (we'll include a template attestation with signature block).
- SLA: 5 business days applies up to 2TB compressed per contract. Above 2TB we will propose a staged export plan (we'll include bandwidth estimate and ETA once we see export size).
- Legal hold: we can place a hold which freezes deletion workflows for specified objects; the hold must be requested in writing and will extend retention until released — we will include the hold in the attestation.

Next steps:
1) Marissa to provision a 24-hour NDJSON sample to Lisa by EOD tomorrow.
2) Rohan to share the S3 role ARN and sample policy.
3) I'll send a short procurement checklist (Drive link) and propose two call times for next week (30 min).

If that all sounds good I'll mark this thread as the primary doc and follow-up with the checklist.

Thanks,

Redwood Inference
